institutionName: Institut d'Etudes Politique de Lyon (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try to live in France because of the culture, language and academic opportunities in Lyon.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international mobility office at Sciences Po has been very helpfull and supportive with answering any of my questions fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed a lot of help with getting courses catalogues and syllabus send beforehand, because the system is a bit different than at UCPH - here you select course after a two week drop-in and -out period, where you have the opportunity to try all different courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me not the easiest part because I looking into it very late. I met a local at training the first week and ended up living with her and her roommates for a while, before I got a student accommodation that I was on waitlist for.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
There is the opportunity to get housing through the host institution, but the spot are limited and there is a strong demand. If interested in this look into "CROUS" - and be early, but also be aware of the location because there are four different locations. I would definitely recommend the one closest to uni, it is convenient and a good area.

Like CROUS there is a lot of student accommodation opportunities if you are early.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Yes, it was easy with the host institution. But it was difficult with UCPH getting any courses approved. I'm still unsure if I get my credits transferred.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a two week drop-in period, where you try out different courses. Afterwards, you select the courses you want. Be aware that some courses might be cancelled - if you expect the courses from last year to reappear.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have a physical office for international students with long oppening hours. And mail of course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes, I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will get the information you need.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were varying in level. Some of the English courses was a bit lower in level - but it seemed like it was because of some of the professeurs' limited English vocabulary and not necessarily the knowledge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is different from they expect way more active participation from the students. Many presentations and class discussions. And it is sometimes part of the final exam grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
"Global Justice"
"European Politics: From Crisis to Renewal"
"Cities and Aspects of Globalization"
"Populism vs. Representative Democracy: A US-French Comparative Approach"
"Persecution, Tolerance and Migration"
"French Politics & Society"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked: "Persecution, Tolerance and Migration"

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Trains to travel fast and cheap. You can go to Paris in two hours or Genève.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of opportunities for sports and hobbies at the university (there is an information-day that I recommend going to).

- And if you like skiing it Lyon is close to the Alpes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you enjoy doing ;)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Parc d'Or, Plage de Grand, South of France before it gets cold, Aix-les-Bains

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is tough with language, but they are really nice. Not French stereotypes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the optional language course and do some sports

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was different, but you are adjust fast.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The long hangouts and willingness to help a stranger

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You will not have "everything in order" before you go - so you have to feel okay about being a bit risky whether it is getting credits transferred, housing, courses or language.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: IMPORTANT: UCPH has been really slow and not so helpful with my reapproval an online learning agreement. I ended my first application in the beginning of January, and I was almost not going because it was so difficult getting courses approved. I ended up going without knowing if I would get my Erasmus Grant or credits transferred afterwards. I have only received first half of grant now in January (after my exchange ended), and I do not believe I get all credits tranferred. They finally approved some of the courses I took this November. This process has taking way too much time and energy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I was worried about the stuff with credits and grants before going, but when I got to Lyon the credits started meaning less because I liked being there so much.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting the courses preapproved and the Erasmus Grant. I recommend going there with masters and not bachelor - bc then you have more flexibility.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
